lines: Concerns regarding menstrual hygiene management during heavy periods causing skin irritation and discomfort, with current menses ongoing for 8 days.

Her mother reports that her daughter has heavy menstrual bleeding and difficulty with personal hygiene during her periods, which has led to skin irritation and discomfort.
Her last menstrual period started 8 days ago and is still ongoing.
Her menstrual cycle is regular, with periods lasting 7-9 days.
The patient has spastic diplegia and is wheelchair-bound.
The patient has a history of iron-deficiency anemia.

lines: History of heavy menstrual bleeding since menarche with periods lasting 7-9 days and frequent nosebleeds and gum bleeding while brushing.

The patient returns to the Obstetrics & Gynecology clinic for continued management of heavy menstrual bleeding, having previously presented for menstrual hygiene concerns and irregular cycles, with established history of mucocutaneous pigmentation and prior hematology evaluation.
She presents with a history of heavy menstrual bleeding since menarche at age 12.
She reports that her menstrual periods last 7-9 days and she often has to change her sanitary products every 2 hours on the heaviest days.
She has experienced episodes of epistaxis, bleeding gums while brushing her teeth, and easy bruising.
There is no family history of bleeding disorders

On physical examination, there is no evidence of anemia.

encounters.cc: Heavy menstrual bleeding with large clots soaking through pads and long-standing history of spontaneous nosebleeds lasting 15-20 minutes.

lines: Heavy menstrual bleeding with large clots soaking through pads and long-standing history of spontaneous nosebleeds lasting 15-20 minutes.
The patient returns to the genetics clinic for continued evaluation of her bleeding symptoms, having been previously assessed in hematology and obstetrics and gynecology.
Her menses are described as heavy since menarche, frequently soaking through pads and often containing large clots.
She also has a long-standing history of spontaneous nosebleeds that can last up to 15–20 minutes and require pressure to stop.
She does not bruise easily and denies any joint swelling or deep muscle pain.
She has not undergone any surgeries or dental extractions.
There is no history of medication use, including anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents.
Her father has experienced similar episodes of recurrent epistaxis throughout his life but was never formally diagnosed with a bleeding disorder.
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: High school student (special education).
Physical exam is unremarkable, with no petechiae or ecchymoses.
Her complete blood count shows a normal hemoglobin and hematocrit.
Her aPTT is within the normal range.
She is referred to hematology for further evaluation of a possible bleeding diathesis.

encounters.cc: Heavy menstrual bleeding requiring simultaneous use of pads and tampons, frequent gum bleeding when brushing, and occasional prolonged nosebleeds.

lines: Heavy menstrual bleeding requiring simultaneous use of pads and tampons, frequent gum bleeding when brushing, and occasional prolonged nosebleeds.
The patient returns to Hematology for ongoing management of bleeding symptoms, having presented previously with similar complaints.
She continues to experience menorrhagia since menarche requiring simultaneous use of pads and tampons.
She reports frequent gum bleeding when brushing her teeth and occasional nosebleeds lasting more than 15 minutes.
She denies joint swelling or prolonged bleeding after minor cuts, but recalls bleeding for several hours after a dental extraction last year.
Her father reports similar symptoms in childhood.
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: High school student (special education).
Physical examination reveals scattered ecchymoses on the arms and legs, but no joint deformities or swelling.
Laboratory testing shows a normal platelet count, normal prothrombin time (PT), and prolonged partial thromboplastin time (PTT).

lines: Heavy vaginal bleeding for 2 days with acute hemorrhage requiring emergency evaluation in the setting of irregular menstrual cycles.
This 20-year-old female with Von Willebrand disease and Peutz-Jeghers syndrome presents to the emergency department with recurrent heavy vaginal bleeding.
She has an established history of menorrhagia with prior hematology and gynecology encounters.
She reports a 2-day history of heavy vaginal bleeding.
She reports that her menstrual cycles have been irregular since menarche at age 13, with intervals ranging from 21 to 45 days.
She denies use of any medications.
